body:
WHAT
`buildSystemPrompt({ env: CANONICAL_ENV })` is rendered and compared byte for byte
against a committed approved artifact at
`tests/approved/system-prompt-is-pinned/system-prompt.txt`. The test NEVER writes that
file. Regenerating it is a separate command a person runs, and the approval is the diff
in the commit.

WHY
The suite pins how MANY prompts exist (46 in 6 groups, 73 once the tool registry is
built) and the ORDER the nine sections compose in. Nothing pins what any of them SAYS.
Reword a behaviour section and every session's instructions change while the suite stays
green. For an agent product the assembled prompt is the product, and it is the one place
where a byte-for-byte snapshot is the correct assertion rather than a brittle one,
because the artifact IS the observable behaviour — the literal text sent to the model.

There is no approval escape hatch on purpose. An `APPROVE=1` mode would let a coding
agent that broke the prompt re-approve its own change and report green, which turns the
guard into a file that costs disk and proves nothing.

WHERE
`engine/core/src/agent/prompts.ts` — `buildSystemPrompt({ env, addons, extraSections })`,
`behaviorCore()`, `environmentBlock(env)` and the `SECTION_*` exports. `PromptEnvironment`
is fully injected (`cwd`, `isGitRepo`, `platform`, `model`, `date`), so the output is
deterministic and needs no scrubbing — which is what makes this cheap.
`engine/protocol/src/prompts.ts` — `overrideText` and `MAGENTRA_PROMPTS_DIR`, which can
replace any prompt (250 ms cache per id) and must be proven absent before the artifact
is trusted.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With no `MAGENTRA_PROMPTS_DIR` set, `buildSystemPrompt` for the canonical environment
   (cwd `/w`, isGitRepo false, platform `win32`, model `m`, date `2026-01-01`) equals
   `tests/approved/system-prompt-is-pinned/system-prompt.txt` byte for byte; on a
   mismatch the failure names the first differing line and prints both sides of it.
2. The approved artifact is non-empty and contains all five values of the environment
   block, so a truncated or emptied artifact can never pass as agreement.
3. With `MAGENTRA_PROMPTS_DIR` pointing at a directory holding one override for a section
   the prompt uses, the test REFUSES to compare and fails naming the override, rather
   than freezing somebody's local edit as the approved text.
4. Called twice in one process with the same canonical environment, `buildSystemPrompt`
   returns identical text — the artifact pins a deterministic function, not one lucky
   ordering.
5. The test writes nothing: its own source names no `writeFileSync`, `appendFileSync` or
   `createWriteStream`, and no environment variable in it selects a rewrite path.

NOTE FOR THE OWNER
`tests/` has no home for committed artifacts today. `tests/approved/<feature-id>/` is the
proposal and a new convention there probably deserves a `decisions/` record. Say if you
want a different location, or the regeneration command named something specific.
